reproduction_target: Study of forkhead (FH) transcription factor DNA bispecificity via protein binding microarrays (PBMs). The reproducible/computational portion covers: (1) FH-domain identification across human TFs (HMMER search against a Pfam-derived pattern) and multiple-sequence alignment (MAFFT L-INS-i) with trimming to a common coordinate system reproducing Pfam PF00250; (2) prioritization/assignment of population and clinical variants by filtering ClinVar and gnomAD onto aligned FH positions; (3) statistical analysis of PBM scan data with the Universal PBM Analysis Suite (GenePix input) yielding 8-mer E-scores, plus a custom specificity-change calling on E-score differences (FKH RYAAAYA vs FHL GACGC, E-score threshold >=0.4); (4) analysis of published FOXN3 ChIP-seq (HepG2 top-2000 peaks from Rogers et al.; MCF-7 reads from GEO GSE93780 mapped to GRCh38 with Bowtie 2, peaks called with MACS2, GC/CpG/promoter/repeat-matched background sets via GENRE, motif-match enrichment tested with Fisher's Exact Test in R), and GO/phenotype enrichment via GREAT version 4. Wet-lab portion (cloning, protein expression, PBM assays) is not the reproduction target here.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool from Methods prose only (stage-1). Mixed paper: wet-lab PBM experimental workflow (cloning, protein expression, array assays) counted as W; computational analyses counted as C-layer steps (S). No Code Availability statement and no GitHub/GitLab/Zenodo/Software Heritage repository is cited anywhere in the manuscript; no analysis scripts are shared. Data Availability names only GEO GSE297784 (the authors' own PBM data). Assessment targets bioRxiv v1 (canonical DOI).

steps.label: FH-domain identification: search canonical UniProt sequences of all human TFs (Lambert et al. TF list) with the HMMER software suite against a Pfam-derived FH pattern; compile FH-domain coordinates per gene
Multiple-sequence alignment of human FH domains with MAFFT (L-INS-i parameter set); trim highly gapped subfamily-specific positions to a common coordinate system reproducing Pfam PF00250 numbering
Variant prioritization/assignment: filter ClinVar and gnomAD variants onto aligned FH positions (49 human FOX genes; UniProt canonical isoforms) to select reference/variant/designed FHs for testing

PBM data statistical analysis: process GenePix scan output with the Universal PBM Analysis Suite ('as described previously') to compute an E-score for every 8-mer per replicate per TF variant/reference

Specificity-change calling: compute variant-minus-reference E-score differences for 8-mers matching FKH (RYAAAYA) or FHL (GACGC) with E-score >=0.4; analyze the difference-score distribution to classify specificity changes (custom analysis)
ChIP-seq read mapping: map MCF-7 FOXN3 ChIP-seq and Input reads (GEO GSE93780) to GRCh38 with Bowtie 2
Peak calling: call FOXN3 peaks with MACS2 using Input as background and default parameters; trim each peak set to 150 bp centered on the summit
Background-set generation: build random background sequence sets matched for G/C content, CpG content, promoter overlap, and repeat content using GENRE
Motif-enrichment testing: count FKH (RYAAAYA) / FHL (GACGC) motif matches in peak vs background sets and assess enrichment significance with Fisher's Exact Test in R
GO-term / phenotype enrichment of motif-containing peak sequence sets using GREAT version 4

headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: NI ceiling on all 10 computational steps. There is NO code-availability statement and no code repository (GitHub/GitLab/Zenodo/Software Heritage) anywhere in the manuscript, and no analysis scripts are shared — every computational step relies on prose-described invocation of standard/external tools (HMMER, MAFFT, Universal PBM Analysis Suite, Bowtie 2, MACS2, GENRE, R/Fisher, GREAT v4) plus a custom PBM specificity-difference analysis. Input data is largely public (UniProt, Lambert TF list, ClinVar, gnomAD, GEO GSE93780, and the authors' PBM data at GEO GSE297784), so the data axis is generally satisfied, but because code=0 for every step the axis-min pins each step to NI regardless of data availability. No environment capture, no software version pins (only GREAT 'version 4' and, as a web service, not env-closing). capture_claim='none' → NOT a stage2 R★/RI candidate; even a perfect stage2 run cannot exceed NI without the analysis code being released.
headline.coverage: 10 computational steps assessed from Methods prose (prose only). Wet-lab experimental workflow counted as W=3 (cloning, protein expression, PBM array assays) and not part of the C-layer readiness score.

gaps.missing: No Code Availability statement and no repository (GitHub/GitLab/Zenodo/Software Heritage) is cited. No analysis scripts are shared for the FH-domain search/alignment/variant-assignment pipeline, the custom PBM E-score specificity-difference analysis, or the ChIP-seq enrichment analysis. The 'Universal PBM Analysis Suite' is referenced only as 'described previously' (citation), not as an obtained, versioned artifact.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the analysis code (domain search/alignment/variant-mapping scripts, PBM E-score processing and specificity-difference calling, ChIP-seq enrichment driver) in a public repository with a tagged release / archive DOI, and add a Code Availability statement referencing the exact commit.

gaps.missing: No environment capture of any kind (no environment.yml / conda-lock / renv.lock / requirements.txt / container). No software versions are pinned for HMMER, MAFFT, Bowtie 2, MACS2, GENRE, or R; GREAT is stated only as 'version 4' (a hosted web service, not an env-closing pin). GenePix software version not stated.
gaps.how_to_close: Provide a lockfile or container digest for a declared platform pinning HMMER, MAFFT, Bowtie 2, MACS2, GENRE, R and the R packages used, plus the exact GREAT version/run date.

gaps.missing: Several steps under-specify parameters: HMMER search options and Pfam pattern derivation (C1), MAFFT trimming/gap thresholds beyond 'L-INS-i' (C2), ClinVar/gnomAD database versions/access dates and filtering criteria (C3), Bowtie 2 mapping parameters (C6), MACS2 stated as 'default parameters' only (C7), GENRE matching configuration (C8), and GREAT run parameters/assembly (C10).
gaps.how_to_close: State exact command lines / parameter sets and database version-dates for each step, ideally embedded in the released analysis scripts.

gaps.missing: MCF-7 FOXN3 ChIP-seq is cited via GEO GSE93780 (resolvable), but HepG2 'top 2000 peaks' are taken from Rogers et al. Supplementary Table S1 rather than a raw-data accession; ClinVar and gnomAD are named without version/download dates. Input protein sequences reference UniProt canonical isoforms and the Lambert et al. TF list without a frozen snapshot.
gaps.how_to_close: Provide accessions or frozen snapshots (with version-dates) for all reused datasets and databases, and a fetch script mapping each to the figures it supports.

gaps.missing: No tagged release or archive DOI exists for any analysis code because no repository is provided at all.
gaps.how_to_close: Create a repository, cite a specific commit/tag, and mint a Zenodo/Software Heritage snapshot referenced from the manuscript.
